etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Medieval Latin tentātīvus (“trying, testing”), from tentō, past participle tentātus (“to try, test”); see tent, tempt.

definitions.definition: A trial; an experiment; an attempt.
(Malaysia) A schedule for an event or a programme.
Of or pertaining to a trial or trials; essaying; experimental.

quote.citation: 2009 May 3, Manohla Dargis, A. O. Scott, “Memos to Hollywood”, in The New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: Meanwhile, a bunch of hungry directors with digital cameras, time on their hands and not much money are making free-form studies about tentative hookups and long conversations among actual, overeducated, undermotivated young folks.

definitions.definition: Restrained; polite; feeling one's way, not using full force.
